title: Descriptive writing
specPoints: Paper 1 Section B: Question 5, the description (AO5 24 marks, AO6 16 marks)

tips.title: Five, thirty-five, five
tips.body: Plan for five minutes, write for thirty-five, check for five. The plan buys the ending, which is the structural feature most pieces lose; the check buys the accuracy marks, which are sixteen of forty.

tips.title: The words of the ladder
tips.body: Compelling and convincing at Level 4, consistent and clear at Level 3. Upper Level 4 is assuredly, sustained, inventive and seamless. Know which word each paragraph is earning.

tips.title: A list is Level 3
tips.body: Describing the picture in the order the eye finds it, however well, is clear and consistent, and stops there. A controlling idea and a focus that moves by design are what lift it.

tips.title: Plan the ending first
tips.body: Write down the image the piece will return to before writing the opening. A cyclical ending is the easiest inventive structure there is, and it is reached only by pieces that knew where they were going.

tips.title: One of each, not four of each
tips.body: One simile that changes the view; one exact verb; one sense beyond sight; one short sentence placed after a long one. Four similes in a paragraph are decoration; one that works is craft.

tips.title: Two scales, checked separately
tips.body: Read the piece once for sense and once for sentences: full stops, commas, apostrophes, the spelling of every ambitious word. The AO6 mark is decided in those five minutes.

why.matters: Description is the writing that makes a reader see, and the exam gives it forty marks because it is the writer's basic craft: choosing an idea, moving the reader's attention through a place, and picking the one exact word. The habits it builds, a controlling idea, a shape planned before the first sentence, a verb that does work, one device that changes the view, five minutes of checking, are the same habits that make any piece of writing land, from a story to a report to a message that has to be understood first time. Reading Mansfield's opening for its craft and then building one's own is how the two halves of Paper 1 teach each other.

examples.title: The first paragraph of anything
examples.body: A travel piece, a product page, the opening of a novel, an estate agent's listing: each begins by making a reader see a place and want to stay in it, and each is built out of the same choices the description task marks. The writer who can open wide and narrow to one thing, and who knows that leaned on the street beats was very hot, is doing the job those writers are paid for.

examples.title: Saying it once, exactly
examples.body: A doctor's note, a set of instructions, a report on what a site looked like when the inspector arrived: writing that has to be understood first time is descriptive writing under discipline. The exact verb, the one detail that carries the scene, the short sentence that stops the reader where they need to stop: the craft the exam rewards is the same craft, with the decoration taken off.

steps.title: Question 5: forty marks for one piece of writing
steps.body:
Section B is one task, worth as much as the four reading questions together. The paper sets a scenario, in June 2024 a magazine asking for contributions to its creative writing section, and gives a choice of two: a description suggested by a picture, or a story from a prompt. The picture in June 2024 was of a very hot place; the story was about a disagreement. The topic is always related to the source in Section A.

**Two sets of marks.** Twenty-four for content and organisation, AO5: what you say and how it is built. Sixteen for technical accuracy, AO6: sentences, punctuation, spelling, vocabulary. The two are marked separately, so a beautifully shaped piece with careless punctuation loses on one scale and not the other.

**Time.** About 45 minutes: five to plan, thirty-five to write, five to check. The front of the paper says to plan, and the AO6 marks are the reason to check.

This topic is the description. The story has its own topic, and technical accuracy has a third.

rows: AO5: ideas, tone, vocabulary, devices, structure, paragraphs
Four levels, each split upper and lower
AO6: sentence demarcation, punctuation, sentence forms, Standard English, spelling, vocabulary
props.title: Forty marks, two scales

visuals.alt: A table of the two mark scales for Question 5: twenty-four for content and organisation and sixteen for technical accuracy, with what each assesses

check.prompt: How are the forty marks for Question 5 divided?
check.solution: AO5, content and organisation, carries twenty-four marks; AO6, technical accuracy, carries sixteen. They are separate scales, so checking for accuracy at the end earns marks that the quality of the ideas cannot.

markScheme.description: Twenty-four for content and organisation, sixteen for technical accuracy, marked on two separate scales

options: Twenty-four for content and organisation, sixteen for technical accuracy, marked on two separate scales
Forty for the writing as a whole, with no separate marks for accuracy, since accuracy is assumed
Twenty for the description and twenty for the story, since both tasks must be attempted by every student
Thirty for the writing and ten for the plan, which the examiners read and mark before the answer itself

steps.title: The content and organisation ladder
steps.body:
AO5 has four levels, and each is split into an upper and a lower band. The words that name them are worth knowing, because they describe what the examiner is reading for.

**Level 4, 19 to 24: compelling, convincing communication.** Upper, 22 to 24: communication is convincing and compelling; tone, style and register assuredly matched to purpose and audience; extensive and ambitious vocabulary with sustained crafting of linguistic devices; varied and inventive structural features; compelling, complex ideas; fluently linked paragraphs with seamlessly integrated discourse markers. Lower, 19 to 21: convincing; convincingly matched; extensive vocabulary with conscious crafting; varied and effective structural features; highly engaging with developed complex ideas; consistently coherent paragraphs.

**Level 3, 13 to 18: consistent, clear communication.** Upper, 16 to 18: consistently clear; increasingly sophisticated vocabulary chosen for effect; effective structural features; engaging with a range of clear, connected ideas; coherent paragraphs with integrated discourse markers. Lower, 13 to 15: generally clear; vocabulary clearly chosen for effect; usually effective structure.

**Level 2, 7 to 12: some successful communication. Level 1, 1 to 6: simple, limited communication.**

Read the descriptors as a list of what to do: match the register, craft the vocabulary, build the structure, connect the paragraphs.

rows: Compelling; register assuredly matched; ambitious vocabulary, sustained crafting
Varied and inventive structure; fluently linked paragraphs
Varied and effective structure; consistently coherent paragraphs
Effective structure; coherent paragraphs, integrated markers
Generally clear; vocabulary chosen for effect
Usually effective structure; usually coherent paragraphs
props.title: Content and organisation, 24 marks

visuals.alt: A table of the AO5 levels for Question 5 with marks, content descriptors and organisation descriptors

check.prompt: Which pair of words does the scheme use for the top of the AO5 ladder?
check.solution: Level 4 is compelling, convincing communication; Level 3 is consistent, clear; Level 2 is some successful; Level 1 is simple, limited. The words are the standard: a Level 3 piece is clear all the way through, and a Level 4 piece makes the reader keep reading.

markScheme.description: Compelling and convincing

options: Clear and consistent throughout
Compelling and convincing
Some and successful in places
Simple and limited in its range

steps.title: The technical accuracy ladder
steps.body:
AO6 has four levels and sixteen marks, and the specification requires it to be a fifth of the whole qualification.

**Level 4, 13 to 16:** sentence demarcation consistently secure and accurate; a wide range of punctuation used with a high level of accuracy; a full range of sentence forms for effect; Standard English used consistently with secure control of complex grammatical structures; a high level of accuracy in spelling, including ambitious vocabulary; extensive and ambitious use of vocabulary.

**Level 3, 9 to 12:** mostly secure demarcation; a range of punctuation mostly successful; a variety of sentence forms for effect; mostly Standard English; generally accurate spelling including complex words; increasingly sophisticated vocabulary.

**Level 2, 5 to 8:** demarcation mostly secure and sometimes accurate; some control of a range of punctuation; attempts a variety of sentence forms. **Level 1, 1 to 4:** occasional demarcation; some conscious punctuation; simple sentence forms.

Notice that sentence forms and vocabulary appear on both scales. A short sentence placed for effect is organisation on AO5 and a sentence form on AO6, and it earns twice.

rows: Every sentence demarcated; a wide range of punctuation, accurate; a full range of sentence forms; ambitious vocabulary spelt right
Mostly secure demarcation; a range of punctuation mostly right; varied sentence forms; complex words spelt right
Demarcation sometimes accurate; some punctuation controlled; some variety attempted
props.title: Technical accuracy, 16 marks

visuals.alt: A table of the AO6 levels for Question 5 with marks and what the examiner sees at each

check.prompt: Why does a short sentence placed for effect count on both scales?
check.solution: AO6 asks for a full range of sentence forms for effect; AO5 asks for varied and inventive structural features. A deliberate short sentence after a long one is both, so it earns on both scales. Vocabulary works the same way: ambitious and spelt right.

markScheme.description: Because sentence forms used for effect are named in the AO6 descriptors and structural features in the AO5 descriptors, so one choice is credited on each

options: Because the examiners mark the piece twice, once for each scale, and count everything twice whether it is a choice or not
Because short sentences are easier to punctuate correctly and so raise the accuracy mark automatically, and the examiners then carry the higher mark across to the content scale as well
Because sentence forms used for effect are named in the AO6 descriptors and structural features in the AO5 descriptors, so one choice is credited on each
Because the AO5 scale rewards anything unusual and the AO6 scale rewards anything correct, and a short sentence is both

steps.title: Planning a description: a shape, not a list
steps.body:
The commonest description is a list of what is in the picture, from left to right, in the order the eye finds it. It is clear, and it is Level 3. A description that reaches the top has a shape, and the shape is the one the Question 3 topic taught for reading, turned round for writing.

**A controlling idea.** One thing the description is about that is not the picture: the heat as a presence with intentions; the place as somewhere that has been waiting; time passing without anything happening. The idea decides what is described and what is left out.

**A focus that moves.** Open wide, then narrow to one thing; or open on one thing and widen. Shift time: a moment later, an hour later. Shift perspective: from outside to inside, from the place to someone in it.

**An ending that returns.** Come back to the first image, changed. A cyclical ending is the easiest inventive structure to build and the one examiners see least.

**Paragraphs with a job each.** Five or six, each one movement of the focus, each opening with a sentence that does the moving.

nodes.text: Open wide, or on one thing

visuals.alt: A flow chart of the shape of a description: a controlling idea, an opening that is wide or close, a narrowing or widening, a shift of time or perspective, and a return to the first image, changed

check.prompt: What separates a description with a shape from a list of what is in the picture?
check.solution: The list describes the picture; the shape describes an idea through the picture, and moves. The AO5 descriptors reward varied and inventive structural features and compelling ideas, and neither is produced by adding adjectives or paragraphs.

markScheme.description: A controlling idea that decides what is described, a focus that moves by design, and an ending that returns to the opening, changed

options: A first-person narrator who explains what they can see in the picture and what they feel about each part of it, so that the reader has a guide through everything in the scene
More adjectives and adverbs in every sentence, so that each thing in the picture is described in as much detail as possible
A larger number of paragraphs, one for each object in the picture, worked through from left to right and top to bottom
A controlling idea that decides what is described, a focus that moves by design, and an ending that returns to the opening, changed

steps.title: A plan and an opening: a very hot place
steps.body: The June 2024 task was a description of a very hot place suggested by a picture. Here is a plan built in five minutes, and the opening it produced.

visuals.problem: Plan a description of a very hot place, then write the opening.

steps.text: Controlling idea: the heat is a landlord. It owns the street, and the people in it are tenants who have stopped arguing.
steps.note: One sentence that is not the picture. Everything else serves it.

steps.text: Shape: open wide on the street at noon; narrow to one shutter and the hand that closes it; shift to the hour before dawn; return to the street, empty, the heat still in charge.
steps.note: Wide, close, time shift, return. Four movements, five paragraphs.

steps.text: Opening paragraph: *Noon owns the street. It has moved in and closed the shutters, one by one, and now it sits in the middle of the road with nothing to do. A dog crosses, thinks better of it, and lies down where it stopped. Nothing else moves. Even the flies have given up flying and hang in the air like something spilt.*
steps.note: The idea in the first sentence; personification held through the paragraph; one simile, doing work; a short sentence for weight.

steps.text: Second paragraph, the narrowing: *At the third window a hand comes out, tests the air as if it were water, and pulls the shutter to.*
steps.note: The focus moves in one sentence, and the sentence does the moving.

steps.text: The return, planned before writing: the last paragraph gives the street back to the noon, with the dog exactly where it was and one shutter open.
steps.note: The ending is decided in the plan, so the piece has somewhere to go.

boxes.title: Devices
boxes.body: Personification held; one simile; one short sentence

boxes.title: Ending
boxes.body: The street given back, one shutter open

visuals.alt: Four boxes showing the plan for a description of a very hot place: the controlling idea, the shape, the devices and the ending

check.prompt: Why does the plan decide the ending before the writing starts?
check.solution: An ending planned is an ending reached. The return to the opening is the inventive structural feature within every student's reach, and it is lost when the piece stops where the time runs out. Five minutes of planning buys the last paragraph.

markScheme.description: So that the piece has somewhere to go and can return to its opening, which is the structural feature the descriptors reward and the one most answers run out of time for

options: So that the piece has somewhere to go and can return to its opening, which is the structural feature the descriptors reward and the one most answers run out of time for
Because a description must always end with the same sentence it began with, and that sentence needs to be written down first
So that the writing can be timed exactly, with the same number of minutes given to each of the paragraphs in the plan
Because the examiners read the ending first and mark the rest of the piece according to how good the last paragraph is, so a strong ending lifts every paragraph before it

steps.title: Crafting the language: precise, not big
steps.body:
The descriptors ask for extensive and ambitious vocabulary with sustained crafting of linguistic devices. Ambitious does not mean long. It means chosen.

**Learn from the opening of Miss Brill.** Mansfield writes “the blue sky powdered with gold”, and the verb does the work: powder is fine, dry and shaken on, which is what that light is. Then “great spots of light like white wine splashed over the Jardins Publiques”: a simile that brings the taste and the carelessness of a splash. Neither word is rare. Both are exact.

**Devices that do work.** One simile that changes how the reader sees the thing beats four that decorate it. Personification held across a paragraph becomes a controlling idea. The senses beyond sight, heat on skin, the sound a place makes when nothing moves, are where most descriptions are thin.

**Sentence forms as craft.** A long sentence that moves with the thing it describes; a short one after it that stops the reader; a list that piles up; a sentence that corrects itself. Vary them on purpose, and the choice earns on both scales.

rows: The sun leaned on the street
The road was like an oven
The road gave the heat back like a debt
The air had a taste, metal and dust
It was so hot that nobody moved at all
props.title: Weak and crafted

visuals.alt: A table contrasting weak and crafted choices in a description: the verb, the simile, the sense and the sentence form

check.prompt: What makes the verb powdered in the blue sky powdered with gold a crafted choice?
check.solution: Ambitious vocabulary is chosen, not rare. Powdered is an everyday word made exact by the thing it describes; the reader sees the light differently because of it. That is the sustained crafting the top descriptor names.

markScheme.description: It is exact: powder is fine, dry and shaken on, which is what that light is, so an ordinary word does the work an unusual one could not

options: It is a verb where the reader expects an adjective, and the surprise is what makes the sentence memorable to a reader who has seen a hundred blue skies described before
It is exact: powder is fine, dry and shaken on, which is what that light is, so an ordinary word does the work an unusual one could not
It rhymes with the sound of the sentence and makes the opening pleasant to read aloud, which the examiners listen for
It is a rare and difficult word that most readers would have to look up, which is what ambitious vocabulary means

steps.title: One paragraph, then the checklist
steps.body:
Write the opening paragraph of a description of a cold place, in ten minutes, from this plan: controlling idea, the cold is patient; open wide; end the paragraph on one short sentence.

Then check it against the list.

1. Is the idea in the first sentence, and not the weather?
2. Is there one verb that does work, and one simile that changes how the reader sees the thing?
3. Is there a sense other than sight?
4. Are the sentence forms varied on purpose, with the short one placed?
5. Is every sentence demarcated and every ambitious word spelt?

Then write the second paragraph so that its first sentence moves the focus.

boxes.title: Idea first
boxes.body: Not the weather: the thing the piece is about

boxes.title: One of each
boxes.body: A verb that works; a simile that changes the view; a sense beyond sight

boxes.title: Forms on purpose
boxes.body: Long that moves; short that stops

visuals.alt: Four boxes giving a checklist for a descriptive paragraph: the idea first, one crafted verb and simile and sense, sentence forms on purpose, and accuracy

check.prompt: Which opening sentence puts the controlling idea first, as the plan asks?
check.solution: The sentence about the cold having all the time in the world gives the reader the idea, the cold as patient, and not the weather report. The others state the weather, begin a narrative, or give a number. A description at the top level is about an idea seen through a place.

markScheme.description: The cold has all the time in the world, and it has decided to spend it here

options: I woke up early and looked out of the window at the frost on the field outside
The temperature was minus ten and the wind was blowing hard from the north
The cold has all the time in the world, and it has decided to spend it here
It was a very cold morning in the middle of winter and there was snow everywhere

steps.title: Compelling: what upper Level 4 has
steps.body:
Lower Level 4 is convincing: the register is right, the vocabulary extensive, the structure varied and effective. Upper Level 4 adds a set of adverbs and adjectives that describe control: tone *assuredly* matched; vocabulary *extensive and ambitious* with *sustained* crafting; structural features *varied and inventive*; ideas *compelling* and *complex*; discourse markers *seamlessly integrated*.

**Assuredly.** The piece never sounds like a student describing a picture for an exam. The register is chosen and held.

**Sustained.** One good simile is conscious crafting; a controlling idea carried through every paragraph is sustained crafting.

**Inventive.** Not the same left-to-right list with better words: a shift of time, a return, a perspective the reader did not expect.

**Seamlessly.** *Meanwhile* and *however* bolted to the front of paragraphs are integrated markers; a paragraph that opens with a sentence that does the moving needs none.

**And the five minutes at the end.** Sixteen marks for accuracy, and Level 4 asks for consistently secure demarcation and a high level of accuracy in spelling. Checking finds the comma splice and the missing letter that would cost the level.

boxes.title: Sustained
boxes.body: The idea carried through every paragraph

boxes.title: Inventive
boxes.body: A shift, a return, a perspective not expected

boxes.title: Seamless
boxes.body: Paragraphs that move without bolted-on markers

visuals.alt: Four boxes on the words of upper Level 4: assuredly, sustained, inventive and seamless

check.prompt: Which change would move a description from lower to upper Level 4?
check.solution: The upper band is about control across the whole piece: sustained crafting, inventive structure, ideas developed rather than multiplied. More devices, more pages and more markers make a piece longer and heavier, not more compelling.

markScheme.description: Carrying the controlling idea through every paragraph and ending with a return to the opening, so the crafting is sustained and the structure inventive

options: Adding two more similes and a metaphor to each paragraph, so that the piece has more linguistic devices than the examiners expect and the crafting is visible in every line
Making the piece longer by a page, so that the extensive vocabulary has more room to appear and be counted
Beginning every paragraph with a discourse marker such as furthermore or moreover, so that the links are visible to the examiner
Carrying the controlling idea through every paragraph and ending with a return to the opening, so the crafting is sustained and the structure inventive

steps.title: The description in one page
steps.body:
Forty marks, one piece, forty-five minutes: five to plan, thirty-five to write, five to check.

- **Two scales:** 24 for content and organisation, 16 for technical accuracy, marked separately.
- **The AO5 words:** compelling and convincing at Level 4; consistent and clear at Level 3; upper Level 4 is assuredly, sustained, inventive, seamless.
- **The AO6 words:** demarcation consistently secure; a wide range of punctuation, accurate; a full range of sentence forms for effect; ambitious vocabulary spelt right.
- **A shape, not a list:** a controlling idea; a focus that moves; a shift of time or perspective; an ending that returns, changed; paragraphs with a job each.
- **Craft, not size:** the exact verb; one simile that changes the view; a sense beyond sight; sentence forms varied on purpose.
- **Plan the ending first,** and keep the five minutes to check.

The story has its own topic; technical accuracy has a third.

rows: Choose the task; write the idea, the shape and the ending
Write five or six paragraphs, each one movement
Check demarcation, punctuation, spelling; fix the ending if it was rushed
props.title: Forty-five minutes

visuals.alt: A summary table of the forty-five minutes for Question 5: five to plan, thirty-five to write, five to check

check.prompt: How many marks are given for technical accuracy in Question 5?
check.solution: Sixteen, on the AO6 scale, against twenty-four for content and organisation. The specification requires technical accuracy to be a fifth of the whole qualification, which is why five minutes of checking is never wasted.

questions.prompt: How many marks are given for content and organisation in Question 5?
questions.solution: 24 marks, AO5, on a scale of four levels each split into upper and lower bands. The remaining 16 are for technical accuracy, which makes the 40 for Section B.
Two tasks, one chosen. In June 2024 the description was of a very hot place suggested by a picture and the story was about a disagreement, both linked to the heat of the source in Section A.

markScheme.description: One of two tasks: a description suggested by a picture, or a story from a prompt, both related to the topic of the reading source

options: One of four tasks: a description, a story, a poem or a letter, on any subject the student chooses, so long as it is suitable for the magazine named in the scenario
No choice: every student writes a description of the picture printed on the paper
One of two tasks: a description suggested by a picture, or a story from a prompt, both related to the topic of the reading source
A choice of picture: two are printed and the student describes whichever they prefer

questions.prompt: What is the term for the words or phrases that link sentences and paragraphs, such as meanwhile, later or however?
questions.solution: Discourse markers. The AO5 descriptors mention them at every level from Level 2 up, from some use of discourse markers at Level 2 to seamlessly integrated discourse markers at the top, where the paragraphs move without a word bolted on the front.

markScheme.description: discourse markers

questions.prompt: About how long should the whole of Question 5 take?
questions.solution: The paper advises about 45 minutes on Section B. Planning is worth five of them because the ending is the structural feature most often lost, and checking is worth five because sixteen marks are for accuracy.

markScheme.description: About 45 minutes: five to plan, thirty-five to write, five to check

options: About 30 minutes, leaving the rest of the paper's time for checking the reading answers
As long as the student needs, since there is no advised time for the writing section
About 60 minutes, since it is worth half the paper and needs more time than the reading
About 45 minutes: five to plan, thirty-five to write, five to check

questions.prompt: Which of these is what the descriptors mean by a structural feature in a piece of writing?
questions.solution: Structure is the shape of the whole: how the focus moves, where time shifts, how the ending sits against the opening. Similes are linguistic devices, long words are vocabulary, full stops are demarcation, and each is credited elsewhere.

markScheme.description: A shift of time or perspective, a narrowing of focus, or an ending that returns to the opening

options: A shift of time or perspective, a narrowing of focus, or an ending that returns to the opening
A simile, a metaphor or a piece of personification used in a sentence to make the description more vivid for the reader
A long word chosen because it is unusual and will impress the examiner
A full stop placed correctly at the end of every sentence in the piece

questions.prompt: What is a controlling idea in a description?
questions.solution: The heat as a landlord; the cold as patient; a place that has been waiting. An idea that is not the picture gives the description something to be about, and a reason to include one thing and leave out another. It is the difference between a list and a piece.

markScheme.description: One thing the piece is about that is not the picture itself, which decides what is described and what is left out

options: The first object in the picture, which must be described before any of the others
One thing the piece is about that is not the picture itself, which decides what is described and what is left out
The mood word in the task, such as hot or cold, which must appear in every paragraph
The narrator's opinion of the place, stated clearly at the end so that the reader knows what to think about everything that has been described

questions.prompt: Why is the sentence Nothing moved. a crafted choice after a long descriptive sentence?
questions.solution: The form does what the content says. A short sentence placed after a long one is deliberate, and both scales reward the deliberateness: varied structural features on one, a full range of sentence forms for effect on the other.

markScheme.description: Because the short form stops the reader as the place has stopped, and it is credited as a structural feature on AO5 and a sentence form for effect on AO6

options: Because the examiners count the sentences and reward pieces with more of them
Because short sentences are always better than long ones in descriptive writing and should be used wherever possible, since the examiners find long sentences hard to follow and mark them down
Because the short form stops the reader as the place has stopped, and it is credited as a structural feature on AO5 and a sentence form for effect on AO6
Because it uses fewer words and so leaves more of the time for the rest of the description

questions.prompt: Put the five minutes of planning in the order the lesson gives them.
questions.solution: Idea, shape, ending, paragraphs. The ending is decided before the paragraphs so that the writing has somewhere to go; a plan that stops at the paragraphs produces a piece that stops where the time runs out.

markScheme.description: the four steps in order

items: Choose the task and write the controlling idea in one sentence
Decide the shape: open wide or close, narrow or widen, shift time or perspective
Decide the ending: the image the piece will return to, changed
Give each paragraph a job, one movement each

questions.prompt: What is the word the top AO5 descriptor uses for tone, style and register that are matched to purpose and audience with complete confidence?
questions.solution: Assuredly: tone, style and register are assuredly matched to purpose and audience. Lower Level 4 says convincingly; Level 3 says clearly. The word describes a piece that never sounds like a student describing a picture for an exam.

markScheme.description: assuredly

questions.prompt: A description works through the picture from left to right, describing each thing well. Where does it sit, and why?
questions.solution: A clear, well-written list is consistently clear communication with effective structure, which is Level 3. Level 4 asks for varied and inventive structural features and compelling ideas, which the list cannot produce however good its sentences.

markScheme.description: Level 3: consistently clear and effective, but the structure is a list rather than a varied and inventive shape, and there is no controlling idea

options: Level 2: because working left to right is a simple structural feature and simple is the Level 2 word
Level 4: describing everything in the picture in order shows thoroughness and control, which the top descriptor rewards as extensive and sustained crafting
Level 1: a description must never follow the order of the picture, and one that does cannot be marked higher
Level 3: consistently clear and effective, but the structure is a list rather than a varied and inventive shape, and there is no controlling idea

questions.prompt: Which revision to an opening sentence moves it towards ambitious vocabulary as the descriptors mean it?
questions.solution: Ambitious vocabulary is chosen for exactness, not size: leaned makes the sun a weight on the street. Piling up adjectives, switching to technical words, or stripping the sentence bare none of them craft it.

markScheme.description: From the sun was very hot to the sun leaned on the street, because the verb is exact and does work an adjective could not

options: From the sun was very hot to the sun leaned on the street, because the verb is exact and does work an adjective could not
From the sun was very hot to the sun was extremely, unbearably, scorchingly hot, because more adjectives means more vocabulary
From the sun was very hot to the solar radiation was intense, because technical words are more ambitious than everyday ones
From the sun was very hot to the sun was hot, because plain words are always better than decorated ones

questions.prompt: Why is an ending that returns to the opening the inventive structural feature within every student's reach?
questions.solution: A cyclical ending costs nothing but foresight. It is a structural choice the reader feels, it shows control across the whole piece, and it is the feature most pieces lack because they stop where the time does. Planning the ending is how it is reached.

markScheme.description: Because it needs only a plan: the first image is written down before the piece begins, and the last paragraph gives it back, changed

options: Because the examiners have a list of approved structures and the return is the first item on it, so every student is expected to use it and is marked down without it
Because it needs only a plan: the first image is written down before the piece begins, and the last paragraph gives it back, changed
Because it lets the student copy the first paragraph again at the end and save time
Because a return means the piece can be as short as two paragraphs, an opening and an ending

questions.prompt: Which assessment objective, worth a fifth of the whole qualification, assesses sentence structures, punctuation and spelling in the writing questions?
questions.solution: AO6: use a range of vocabulary and sentence structures for clarity, purpose and effect, with accurate spelling and punctuation. Sixteen marks on each paper, and the specification requires it to be twenty per cent of the qualification.

markScheme.description: AO6

questions.prompt: These four sentences describe the same street. Put them in the order that opens wide, narrows, shifts time and returns.
questions.solution: Wide, close, a shift of time, the return. The order is the shape, and the shape is what the AO5 descriptors call varied and inventive structural features; the same four sentences in another order would be a list.

markScheme.description: the four sentences in order

items: Noon owns the street, and nothing in it moves
At the third window a hand comes out, tests the air, and pulls the shutter to
An hour before dawn the street was a different colour and belonged to nobody
By noon the street is the noon's again, with one shutter open

questions.prompt: Write the opening two paragraphs of a description of a very hot place, as suggested by a picture of an empty street at midday. Plan first: a controlling idea, a wide opening, and a second paragraph whose first sentence narrows the focus. Craft the language: one exact verb, one simile that changes how the reader sees the thing, one sense beyond sight, and a short sentence placed for effect.
questions.solution:
Noon owns the street. It has moved in and closed the shutters one by one, and now it sits in the middle of the road with nothing to do. A dog crosses, thinks better of it, and lies down where it stopped. The air has a taste, metal and dust, and it does not so much move as lean, the way a crowd leans when it has nowhere to go. Even the flies have given up flying and hang in the air like something spilt. Nothing moves.

At the third window a hand comes out, tests the air as if it were water, and pulls the shutter to. Behind it a room goes dark and the dark is the coolest thing for a mile. The hand is old; it has done this every day of a long life at exactly this hour, and it does it without looking, the way a hand turns off a tap. For a moment the street has a witness. Then the latch drops, and the noon has the road to itself again, and the dog, which lifted its head for the sound, lets it fall.

markScheme.description: idea first and held
the focus moved by a sentence
crafted language
accuracy

criteria.text: The controlling idea is in the first sentence and is held through both paragraphs, not the weather but an idea seen through the place
The second paragraph opens with a sentence that moves the focus, so the structure is built rather than listed
The language is crafted: an exact verb, one working simile, a sense beyond sight, and a short sentence placed for effect
Every sentence is demarcated, punctuation is accurate and varied, and ambitious words are spelt correctly

questions.prompt: Write a plan and the final paragraph of a description of a cold place, so that the ending returns to the opening image, changed. Give the plan in four lines: controlling idea, shape, devices, ending. Then write the last paragraph, about 120 words, so that a reader who had read the opening would recognise the return.
questions.solution:
Plan. Idea: the cold is patient, and it can wait longer than anything alive. Shape: open on the frozen field at first light, wide; narrow to a single fence post with the frost growing on it; shift to a figure crossing the field and the sound the ground makes; return to the post at dusk. Devices: the cold personified and held through the piece; one simile for the frost; the sense of sound. Ending: the post again, the frost thicker, the figure gone.

Final paragraph. By dusk the post has grown its second coat. The frost that was a breath on it at first light has thickened to fur, and it stands in the field like something that has decided to stay. The footprints that crossed at noon are already filling; by morning the field will not remember them, and the cold will not have noticed. It does not need to. It has the night, and the one after that, and it has never once been in a hurry. Somewhere behind the hedge a door closes, small and far, and the sound goes out across the field and is taken. The post keeps its coat. The cold keeps its patience.

markScheme.description: the plan
the return, changed
crafted language, register held
accuracy

criteria.text: The plan has a controlling idea that is not the weather, a shape with a shift, and an ending decided in advance
The final paragraph returns to the opening image and shows it changed, so the structure is cyclical
The language is crafted and the register held: exact verbs, one working device, a sense beyond sight
The paragraph is accurate: demarcated, punctuated, spelt

questions.prompt: A student writes a compelling description but leaves no time to check it, and it has four comma splices and three misspelt ambitious words. What happens to the marks?
questions.solution: The scales are separate. Content and organisation can be rewarded at Level 4 while technical accuracy sits at Level 3 or below. Five minutes of checking is the cheapest way to earn marks on the whole paper.

markScheme.description: The AO5 mark can still be high, but the AO6 mark falls below Level 4, which needs consistently secure demarcation and accurate spelling

options: Nothing happens, because the examiners are told to ignore errors in an otherwise compelling piece
The AO5 mark falls and the AO6 mark stays, because errors are a failure of content
The AO5 mark can still be high, but the AO6 mark falls below Level 4, which needs consistently secure demarcation and accurate spelling
Both marks fall to Level 1, because a piece with that many errors cannot be compelling, and the examiners are told to mark the two scales together when the accuracy is poor

questions.prompt: A student says: 'A description has no story, so it has no structure; I just describe what I see.' What is the better account?
questions.solution: Structure is movement and shape, not plot. The Question 3 features of reading, focus shifts, time shifts, perspective, a cyclical return, are the structural features of writing, and the description that has them reaches the level the list cannot.

markScheme.description: A description is structured by where the focus goes, when time shifts and how the ending answers the opening, and the AO5 descriptors reward that shape as varied and inventive structural features

options: The student is right: structure belongs to stories, and a description is marked only on its vocabulary and its devices
A description has structure only if it is written in the order of the picture, from left to right and top to bottom
A description should be given a story so that it has a structure, with characters, a plot and a twist at the end, since that is what the examiners understand by structure
A description is structured by where the focus goes, when time shifts and how the ending answers the opening, and the AO5 descriptors reward that shape as varied and inventive structural features

examTechnique.body:
**One task, forty marks, about 45 minutes.** Choose fast, plan for five, write for thirty-five, check for five.

**Two scales.** 24 for content and organisation, 16 for technical accuracy, marked separately. The check at the end is where the second scale is decided.

**A shape, not a list.** A controlling idea in the first sentence; a focus that moves by design; a shift of time or perspective; an ending that returns, changed. Plan the ending before the opening.

**Craft, not size.** The exact verb; one simile that changes how the reader sees; a sense beyond sight; sentence forms varied on purpose, with the short one placed.

**The register held.** The piece should never sound like a student describing a picture for an exam. Assuredly is the top descriptor's word.
examinerErrors: Describing the picture from left to right as a list, which is clear and consistent and stops at Level 3.
Piling up adjectives and similes in place of choosing one exact word and one working device.
Running out of time before the ending, so the piece stops rather than returns.
Leaving the whole piece unchecked and losing the AO6 level to comma splices and misspelt ambitious words.
Beginning with the weather rather than an idea, so the register is never established.
Slipping into a story with characters and events when the task asked for a description.
examTechnique.grade9Looks: A grade 9 description is about an idea seen through a place, and the idea is in its first sentence. The focus moves by design, wide then close, or close then wide, with a shift of time or perspective, and the ending returns to the opening image, changed, because the plan decided it would. The vocabulary is exact rather than large, the devices are few and each does work, a sense beyond sight is present, and the sentence forms are varied on purpose, the short ones placed. Every sentence is demarcated, the punctuation is wide and accurate, and the ambitious words are spelt, because five minutes were kept to check.
